SDP.Journal.Career.merchant.Title: Merchants
SDP.Journal.Career.merchant.Epigraph1: "Trade is the art of turning trust into profit."
SDP.Journal.Career.merchant.Intro:
Merchants travel roads and markets to exchange goods and information.

Their reputation and network are worth as much as their purse.
SDP.Journal.Career.investigator.Title: Investigators
SDP.Journal.Career.investigator.Epigraph:
"When I arrived at the scene, everyone blamed the miller's son. An hour later, I noticed mud stains under the magistrate's boots. Three days after that, he confessed everything. The guilty fear swords; I prefer questions."
— Elarion Sylwen, Detective
SDP.Journal.Career.investigator.Intro:
Investigators devote their lives to uncovering the truth, whether it lies hidden behind a lie, a murder, or a conspiracy. Accustomed to noticing what others overlook, they gather clues, testimony, and rumors to reconstruct events with precision.

Some work for authorities, guilds, or nobility, while others practice their trade independently, hiring out their services to whoever can afford them. A good investigator knows that answers are rarely found at first glance and that the most insignificant details are often the most revealing.

In a world filled with secrets, corruption, and false appearances, their patience, insight, and determination are their most valuable weapons.
SDP.Journal.Career.duellist.Title: Duellists
SDP.Journal.Career.duellist.Epigraph1:
"I saw that fellow enter the arena with a sword, a shield, two daggers, and a bow on his back. I thought he couldn't choose his weapon. After watching him defeat three opponents with each of them, I understood he had chosen them all."
— Durgan, veteran of the Gralnik clan Pits
SDP.Journal.Career.duellist.Intro:
Duellists live for combat and confrontation. Where others fight out of duty, necessity, or greed, they seek above all the test of strength and the refinement of their art. Whether in a duel of honor, a fight in a crowded arena, or an impromptu clash on a lonely road, they see every opponent as a chance to learn and push their limits.

Unlike many warriors who specialize in a single weapon or style, duellists cultivate great versatility. Swords, axes, spears, daggers, bows, or exotic weapons—they strive to master whatever can give them an edge in a fight. For them, each weapon teaches a different lesson, and every defeat is a chance to improve.

Over their travels, duellists face champions, veterans, gladiators, and masters-at-arms in hopes of forging their reputation. Some seek glory, others fortune, but all share the same certainty: there is always a more formidable opponent somewhere, and they must be found.
SDP.Journal.Career.guard.Title: Guards
SDP.Journal.Career.guard.Epigraph1:
The Gardener

A noble once mocked a guard who spent his time watching the palace gardens.
— "Are you guarding flowers now?"
The guard replied:
"The flowers teach me what changes."

A few days later, he discovered that a spy was using the garden to pass messages.

Since then, some guards say:
"Those who ignore the details protect the problems."
— Eldran Loranis
SDP.Journal.Career.guard.Intro:
Guards are the protectors of roads, cities, estates, and those who can afford their services. Some swear fealty to a lord, others serve a city, a merchant company, or a guild. A few simply sell their skills to the highest bidder.

Their role varies enormously. A guard may watch a city's gates, escort a caravan through hostile lands, keep order in a rowdy tavern, or defend a noble's home against assassins and thieves.

Unlike soldiers, guards rarely fight on a battlefield. Their daily life is one of waiting, vigilance, and quick decisions when trouble arises. They learn to recognize suspicious behavior, defuse conflicts before they escalate, and survive situations where the rules suddenly cease to apply.

Many consider the trade thankless. Guards are often the first to receive insults and the last to receive thanks. Yet when gates give way, when bandits attack, or when a crowd grows uncontrollable, they are the ones who stand between danger and those they protect.
SDP.Journal.Career.soldier.Title: Soldiers
SDP.Journal.Career.soldier.Epigraph1:
"When the battle ends, everyone remembers the general's name. Yet it was the anonymous soldiers who bore the weight of victory on their shoulders."
— Naeril, Recruit
SDP.Journal.Career.soldier.Intro:
Soldiers are the pillars of every organized armed force. Whether they serve a realm, a city, a free company, a guild, or a wealthy patron, they share the same ideal: discipline. Where adventurers improvise and mercenaries sometimes follow their instincts, the soldier acts according to training, formation, and the orders given to them.

Their apprenticeship goes far beyond simply mastering weapons. They learn to fight in formation, cover their companions, keep their composure under pressure, and carry out their mission despite fatigue or fear. Many know how to provide first aid, recognize favorable ground, or hold a battle line when all seems lost.

As they gain experience, many choose to specialize in a particular field. Some develop their leadership qualities to direct their companions on the battlefield, while others become skilled marksmen capable of bringing down a target at long range. A few devote their knowledge to healing the wounded in the thick of combat, while others specialize in fighting cavalry by wielding long weapons meant to break charges. Finally, the sturdiest don heavy armor and become living bulwarks, able to withstand the fiercest assaults to protect their allies.

Over the course of campaigns, soldiers acquire experience that no training can replace. They learn to read an opponent's intentions, coordinate a group's movements, and make swift decisions when orders can no longer be relayed. The most capable naturally become figures of authority, able to turn a disparate troop into a disciplined force.

Whether they defend a fortress's ramparts, escort convoys through hostile lands, or lead their companions into the heart of battle, soldiers embody an army's strength. Their true weapon is not their sword or their shield, but the trust their allies place in them when combat turns chaotic.
SDP.Journal.Career.player.Title: Totebol Players
SDP.Journal.Career.player.Epigraph1:
"One day, someone asked why the elves had invented a sport where people could hit each other. The old master replied: 'Because a warrior who knows only strength wins duels, but a warrior who knows strategy wins wars.'"
— Aerendil the Strategist
SDP.Journal.Career.player.Intro:
Totebol has its origins among the elves, long before it became the sport we know today. At that time, it was not a game, but a military exercise designed to train warriors for group combat. Two teams faced each other while each protected a totem representing their leader. The objective was simple: open a breach in the enemy lines to reach the opposing totem and plant a knife into it, while preventing the other team from doing the same.

This training developed far more than throwing skill. Fighters learned to cover their allies, create openings, anticipate enemy movements, and act as a single unit. Victory rarely went to the strongest or fastest, but to those able to coordinate their efforts and seize the slightest weakness in the enemy defense.

Over the centuries, this martial exercise left the training camps and became a sporting discipline. Knives were replaced by a ball, and the rules evolved to preserve the spirit of the exercise while limiting deadly risks. Blows remained allowed, recalling Totebol's military origins, but were gradually regulated to leave as much room for technique as for physical commitment.

Today, Totebol is played in most realms and draws considerable crowds. Behind every pass, tackle, and shot lies a heritage several centuries old. While spectators come to admire spectacular plays, connoisseurs know that the greatest matches are won above all through strategy, coordination, and trust between players.
SDP.Journal.Career.bountyhunter.Title: Bounty Hunters
SDP.Journal.Career.bountyhunter.Epigraph:
"A trail always ends somewhere. Usually in front of me."
— Thorek the Predator
SDP.Journal.Career.bountyhunter.Intro:
Criminals, deserters, bandits, and murderers spend their lives running. Bounty hunters spend theirs tracking them down.

Unlike guards or soldiers, they do not necessarily serve an authority. Some work for lords, cities, or merchant guilds, while others operate alone, guided only by the promise of a reward. Whether the target is a wanted thief, a fugitive assassin, or a monster terrorizing the roads, it matters little so long as a bounty is offered.

The trade demands far more than fighting skill. A good bounty hunter must know how to follow a trail, question witnesses, recognize a lie, survive in the wild, and identify their prey's habits. The most experienced claim that the hunt begins long before combat; when a target is found, half the work is already done.

Few appreciate their presence. Criminals fear them, authorities tolerate them, and honest folk never truly know whether they are agents of justice or mere mercenaries drawn by gold. Yet when someone must be found, alive or dead, it is often to them that people turn.
SDP.Journal.Career.heretichunter.Title: Heretic Hunters
SDP.Journal.Career.heretichunter.Epigrap:
"Every magical catastrophe begins with someone who claims to know what they are doing."
— Lorien Althéa
SDP.Journal.Career.heretichunter.Intro:
Few individuals choose this path by chance.

Most Heretic Hunters have seen magic destroy a life, a family, or an entire community. Some lost loved ones in a ritual gone wrong. Others survived an uncontrolled arcane experiment or the consequences of a mage who believed themselves wiser than the rest of the world.

Where others see a tool, they see a danger.
Where others admire power, they remember the price to be paid.

Heretic Hunters track cultists, necromancers, and all those whose practices threaten the established order. They investigate disappearances, strange phenomena, and rumors of witchcraft. They learn to recognize forbidden symbols, the lies of initiates, and the traces left by the occult arts.

Not all serve the same authority. Some work for lords, cities, or specialized organizations. Others act as independent agents, selling their services to those who fear the dangers of magic. Whatever their allegiance, they often share the same conviction:
Magic is a power too dangerous to be left unsupervised.

For many, this career also represents the only legal way to oppose mages. Where an ordinary man would be hanged for assaulting a sorcerer, a Heretic Hunter possesses the authority needed to investigate, arrest, and sometimes execute those they judge responsible for putting others in danger.

This authority attracts idealists and fanatics alike.
For between protecting the world from the dangers of magic and persecuting those who practice it, the line is sometimes thinner than a razor's edge.
SDP.Journal.Career.priest.Title: Priests of Omira
SDP.Journal.Career.priest.Epigraph1:
"Men fear storms because they are visible. The wise fear imbalances, for they grow in silence."
— Aerendil, Grand Priest
SDP.Journal.Career.priest.Intro:
Omira is the goddess of the world itself. She is neither the goddess of a people nor of a kingdom, but of the earth that bears all life. Her faithful believe that every creature, every forest, every mountain, and every river is part of a fragile balance that must be preserved.

The priests of Omira teach moderation above all else. The pleasures of existence are not condemned; they are even considered a natural part of life. However, any form of excess is seen as a threat to balance. Greed, unchecked ambition, gratuitous violence, or the relentless pursuit of power always end in suffering and destruction.

This philosophy also extends to individual responsibility. The faithful of Omira believe that every action has consequences, whether visible or not. When a serious fault goes unpunished or its author escapes the repercussions of their acts, it is not uncommon for priests to impose or practice acts of self-flagellation and penance themselves. These rituals are not meant to satisfy any cruelty, but to remind that no one can forever escape the consequences of their choices. Voluntary suffering then becomes a means of acknowledging one's fault, accepting its weight, and symbolically restoring the broken balance.

Their role extends far beyond that of simple spiritual guides. As advisors, scholars, healers, diplomats, or interpreters of omens, they seek to understand the signs left by Omira and preserve the harmony of the world. Many study divination to observe echoes of the past, possible paths of the future, or events unfolding far from their sight.

Although they do not condemn magic as a whole, the priests of Omira are particularly cautious toward arts they judge capable of breaking the natural balance. Certain forms of magic, certain artifacts, and certain ancient stones are kept under constant watch. The most dangerous are sometimes hidden, confiscated, or kept secret, even when the reasons for these prohibitions are not revealed to the rest of the world.

Their influence remains primarily concentrated in Reselune, where the head of the faith and the lord of the cult reside. Yet for some time now, the cult has sought to extend its influence beyond its borders. Some see a sincere will to protect the world. Others suspect the priests of seeking to conquer new regions through their faith.
SDP.Journal.Career.battlemage.Title: Battle Mages
SDP.Journal.Career.battlemage.Epigraph1:
"A soldier carries a blade. A Battle Mage carries a storm."
— Aelion, Arcane Ravager
SDP.Journal.Career.battlemage.Intro:
Magic can change the course of a battle. A handful of well-trained mages is sometimes enough to bring down a fortification, repel an army, or save a besieged city. For this reason, most kingdoms seek to train and oversee their own Battle Mages.

Unlike scholars who spend their lives in libraries or research towers, Battle Mages learn their art amid military camps, forced marches, and battlefields. They must be capable of casting a spell under a rain of arrows, maintaining their concentration despite the din of combat, and surviving the many magical catastrophes that inevitably accompany war.

Although some sell their services as mercenaries, most serve their homeland with loyalty. They are often regarded as strategic weapons as much as soldiers, and their presence alone may be enough to discourage an invasion or break an enemy's will before hostilities even begin.

Their training is demanding. A Battle Mage must master the magical arts while learning military discipline, camp life, war tactics, and cooperation with ordinary soldiers. The most talented eventually lead their own units, or even entire battalions of mages capable of unleashing forces that few adversaries can hope to face.

For many, they represent the pride and power of their nation. For others, they are nothing more than living weapons whose next mistake could cost hundreds of lives.
SDP.Journal.Career.scholar.Title: Scholars
SDP.Journal.Career.scholar.Epigraph1:
"The ignorant believe that knowledge lies in books. The wise know it resides in the questions those books lead us to ask."
— Caladriel Faelwyn, Professor of the Archives of Orlayon
SDP.Journal.Career.scholar.Intro:
Scholars devote their lives to research, study, and the preservation of knowledge. Where others pursue wealth or glory, they seek understanding of the world and the mysteries that surround it. Whether history, ancient languages, philosophy, natural sciences, or forgotten traditions, no subject is unworthy of their curiosity.

Much of their time is spent consulting manuscripts, comparing contradictory accounts, translating ancient texts, or recording their discoveries for future generations. Many work in libraries, universities, academies, or in the service of powerful patrons eager to access their expertise.

Scholars are also often called upon to teach their knowledge. As professors, tutors, or lecturers, they pass on what they know to those who wish to learn, convinced that knowledge is worth little unless it is preserved and shared. They are the silent guardians of the heritage of peoples.
SDP.Journal.Career.engineer.Title: Engineers
SDP.Journal.Career.engineer.Epigraph1:
"When the smoke cleared, nothing remained of the tower but a smoking crater. I asked Brokk if his experiment had failed. He looked at me as if I were an idiot and replied: 'Of course not. Now I know what not to do.'"
— Kazrik of Clan Gralnik
SDP.Journal.Career.engineer.Intro:
Dwarf engineers are the undisputed masters of mechanics, gunpowder, and machinery. Where others see a heap of metal, gears, and pipes, they see a solution to a problem or an invention waiting to be born. From the depths of their fortresses to the battlefield, they devote their lives to designing, building, and perfecting machines capable of accomplishing what brute strength alone never could.

Their knowledge is the fruit of generations of experimentation, meticulous calculation, and, it must be admitted, a considerable number of explosions. Cannons, repeating weapons, drills, mine lifts, and complex mechanisms — dwarf engineers constantly push the limits of technology despite often rudimentary means. They treat every failure as a valuable lesson and every catastrophe as an opportunity to improve their designs.

It is not uncommon for an engineer to bear burns, scars, or a partially singed beard, souvenirs of particularly ambitious experiments. Yet these mishaps never seem to dampen their enthusiasm. To a dwarf engineer, an invention that has never exploded has probably never been properly tested.
SDP.Journal.Career.thief.Title: Thieves
SDP.Journal.Career.thief.Epigraph1:
"The lord claimed no one could break into his safe. I left him a note inside to congratulate him on his confidence."
— Aelarion Faelwen, Master Thief
SDP.Journal.Career.thief.Intro:
Thieves live in the gaps of society, where laws are bent and opportunities seized before they vanish. Some content themselves with relieving inattentive passers-by of their purses, while others break into the best-guarded homes to take objects their owners believed safe from any covetous hand.

Unlike the image of the simple brigand, the finest thieves must show great intelligence, remarkable patience, and an excellent capacity for adaptation. They learn to observe their targets' habits, spot weaknesses in a security system, and disappear before their misdeed is even discovered.

Theft is as much an art as a crime. Some practice it out of necessity, others for money, adrenaline, or the challenge of a target reputed inaccessible. Whatever their motivation, thieves share the same certainty: a lock is merely an invitation, and every well-guarded treasure deserves an attempt to steal it.
SDP.Journal.Career.brigand.Title: Brigands
SDP.Journal.Career.brigand.Intro:
Brigands live at the expense of others. Whether they lay ambushes on the roads, ransom travelers, rob passers-by in alleys, or take advantage of chaos to plunder, all share the same goal: to grow rich without obeying the law.

Their methods are as varied as their victims. Some prefer threats and intimidation, others rely on stealth, swindling, or carefully prepared ambushes. Many operate in small groups, but the most ambitious end up leading true bands capable of controlling a district, a forest, or a stretch of road.

Little do they care whether their reputation inspires fear or contempt. So long as purses stay full and the authorities arrive too late, the trade continues to pay.
SDP.Journal.Career.swindler.Title: Swindlers
SDP.Journal.Career.swindler.Epigraph1:
"The secret is not to lie... it is to let the other person build the lie for you."
— Dromli
SDP.Journal.Career.swindler.Intro:
Not all criminals live by the sword. Some prefer cards, dice, false smiles, and fine words. Swindlers make their fortune by exploiting their victims' greed, naivety, or desperation. Whether they sell miracle cures, counterfeit relics, forged property deeds, or purported magical objects, they always know how to find someone willing to pay.

The most modest frequent taverns, markets, and fairs, living off rigged bets, small schemes, and petty thefts. Others travel the roads with a cart full of dubious-quality goods, regularly changing their name and region so as never to cross the same victims twice.

Over time, some perfect their art by forging false documents, counterfeit coin, or imitated seals with remarkable precision. The most talented become true masters of manipulation, capable of swindling a simple peasant, a wealthy merchant, or even a representative of the authorities.

For a swindler, violence is rarely the best solution. A purse obtained through lies draws less attention than one snatched by force. After all, a victim convinced they struck an excellent deal will sometimes return on their own... with even more money.
SDP.Journal.Career.attendant.Title: Employees
SDP.Journal.Career.attendant.Epigraph1:
"When I was young, I asked my master why he greeted every worker on our estate by name. He replied: 'Because a house does not stand thanks to its stones, but thanks to the hands that maintain them.' That day, I understood that a good steward knows his buildings... but a great steward knows his people."
— Memoirs of Elandril
SDP.Journal.Career.attendant.Intro:
Employees are the indispensable cogs of cities. They load carts, serve customers, maintain buildings, care for animals, transport goods, and perform a thousand other tasks without which neither shops nor workshops could function.

Most begin as simple clerks, performing the most thankless work under a superior's orders. With experience, they earn their employers' trust and are entrusted with greater responsibilities. Some end up leading a team, managing stock, or supervising an entire establishment.

Whether they work in an inn, a shop, public baths, a warehouse, a port, or the stables of a wealthy owner, employees develop a remarkable capacity for adaptation. Accustomed to dealing with every layer of society, they know how to treat with customers as well as suppliers, listen to the gossip circulating in town, and solve the small problems of daily life.

The best become stewards. Charged with administering an establishment, they manage staff, day-to-day finances, and relations with customers or suppliers. Though their names are rarely known to the general public, they are often the true architects of their master's affairs running smoothly... or their own.
SDP.Journal.Career.sailor.Title: Sailors
SDP.Journal.Career.sailor.Epigraph1:
"A map never replaces the experience of the one who holds it."
— Caladrel the Navigator
SDP.Journal.Career.sailor.Intro:
Sailors spend their lives on the water, whether on rivers, lakes, or the most distant seas. They carry goods, travelers, soldiers, or fishermen, facing currents, storms, and the dangers that accompany every voyage on a daily basis.

Life aboard is demanding. Everyone must know how to handle a vessel, climb the rigging, repair damage, hold a course, or simply perform the countless tasks required to keep a ship running. Long days of labor, nights spent on deck, and sometimes extreme conditions forge particularly hardy men and women.

Through long travels on waterways, sailors develop a keen sense of observation and orientation. They learn to read winds, currents, and changes in weather, but also to recognize ports, coastlines, and the hazards along their route. Many know countless tales, songs, and legends passed from crew to crew over the course of their voyages.

Whether they sail alone in a modest river skiff or command an imposing merchant vessel, all share the same reality: on the water, the slightest mistake can have dramatic consequences, and only experience brings crew and cargo safely to port.
SDP.Journal.Career.diplomat.Title: Diplomats
SDP.Journal.Career.diplomat.Epigraph1:
"If you know a man's language, you can speak to him. If you know his people, you can persuade him."
— Elarion the Negotiator
SDP.Journal.Career.diplomat.Intro:
Diplomats are the voices of those they represent. Whether they serve a kingdom, a free city, a merchant guild, a religious order, or a powerful noble family, their role is to defend their employer's interests through words rather than arms.

Their daily lives are filled with negotiations, receptions, treaties, and meetings where every word matters. A simple misunderstanding can spark a war, while a well-chosen phrase can end years of conflict. They learn to read their interlocutors' intentions, recognize lies, spot weaknesses, and find compromise when all seems lost.

But a diplomat does not spend life only in palaces. The roads are part of the trade. They travel from one court to another, escort delegations, carry confidential messages, and represent their sovereign in sometimes hostile lands. The best know how to adapt to every culture, speak several languages, and understand the customs of many nations.

While some see them as mere negotiators, others know they can be formidable adversaries. A war avoided through a few words is often a far greater victory than one won on a battlefield.
SDP.Journal.Career.intendant.Title: Stewards
SDP.Journal.Career.intendant.Epigraph1:
"Peasants think I come for their coin. They forget that without that coin, there would be no mill, no bridge, and soon no harvests left to protect."
— Elaith the Receiver
SDP.Journal.Career.intendant.Intro:
Stewards are the guardians of the property and interests of those they serve. Whether they work for a lord, a guild, a temple, a wealthy merchant family, or a city, they ensure the proper functioning of the estates entrusted to them.

Their trade is not limited to keeping ledgers. They travel the land to inspect harvests, collect taxes and dues, settle minor disputes, supervise employees, and ensure that every coin is spent correctly. They must know how to negotiate with a merchant as well as bring a recalcitrant farmer to order or organize the rebuilding of a bridge swept away by floods.

With experience, their responsibilities extend far beyond a single estate. The most capable administer vast properties, manage a guild's finances, oversee several holdings, or become their employer's principal representatives. The greatest among them govern immense territories or administer powerful institutions, where the slightest decision may affect the lives of thousands.

While many consider soldiers the strength of a kingdom, stewards know that no army marches for long without provisions, without taxes, and without an administration capable of sustaining the war effort.
SDP.Journal.Career.courtesan.Title: Pleasure Houses
SDP.Journal.Career.courtesan.Epigraph1:
"When I was young, I believed our house sold pleasure. It took me years to understand that we mostly sold attention. Merchants came to speak of their affairs, captains of their battles, priests of their doubts, and nobles of their ambitions. I listened more than I answered. One evening, an old man whispered to me that whoever knows the desires of a city already holds half its power. Many years later, when I opened my own house, I finally understood he was right. The greatest profits never came from the rooms, but from the conversations that preceded them."
— Excerpt from the memoirs of Phila, Mistress of the House
SDP.Journal.Career.courtesan.Intro:
Pleasure houses are far more than simple places of debauchery. Deals are struck there, secrets exchanged, alliances forged, and confidences heard that even the most trusted advisors never learn. Those who work there quickly discover that words, glances, and silences are sometimes worth more than a well-honed blade.

While some earn their living by offering companionship, the most skilled know how to entertain, seduce, and put everyone at ease. They cultivate the arts, music, dance, or conversation to satisfy an ever more demanding clientele. Over time, they become sought-after intermediaries, able to introduce the right people, arrange discreet meetings, or obtain information that no purse could buy.

The most influential eventually run their own house. They recruit staff, maintain a vast network of contacts, and ensure their establishment remains a safe, refined, and profitable place. Behind the smiles and festivities often hide shrewd negotiators whose influence extends far beyond the walls of their house.
SDP.Journal.Career.doctor.Title: Doctors
SDP.Journal.Career.doctor.Epigraph1:
"The ignorant believe that medicine consists of saving lives. The truth is that it consists of understanding how they work. What each person does with that knowledge is a matter of conscience."
— Vaelor Nythren, anatomist
SDP.Journal.Career.doctor.Intro:
Doctors devote their lives to the study of the body, disease, and injury. Whether they practice in a great city, a renowned university, or the heart of an isolated village, they seek to understand the mechanisms of life in order to preserve it better. Their knowledge is precious, for few professions demand as much learning, patience, and precision.

Some lead a peaceful existence in a practice or academy, receiving patients and students while enriching their research. Others prefer to travel the world, accompanying expeditions, armies, or caravans to study unknown creatures, discover new diseases, or bring aid to communities without access to care.

The study of anatomy often leads doctors to take an interest in all forms of life. Many collect notes, sketches, and observations on the peoples and creatures they encounter, convinced that every discovery may save lives in the future.

However, medical knowledge is not always used for benevolent ends. Some doctors use their expertise to manipulate, poison, or experiment on their fellow beings. For those who know how to heal also know the most effective ways to harm. Thus doctors are sometimes regarded with as much respect as suspicion.
SDP.Journal.Career.hunter.Title: Hunters
SDP.Journal.Career.hunter.Epigraph1:
"My apprentice asked me how I had found the deer. I told him I had not found it. I had found its trail, its territory, its habits, and its next watering hole. The deer was merely the conclusion."
— Thaelar Velys, Sylvaris hunter
SDP.Journal.Career.hunter.Intro:
Hunters live among forgotten trails, silent undergrowth, and vast wild expanses where few dare venture. They track game for meat, fur, or trophies, supplying villages and travelers with resources only nature can provide. Their survival depends as much on their skill as on their knowledge of the wild.

Over the years, hunters learn to read traces left in the mud, recognize a predator's cry from leagues away, and distinguish signs heralding a storm or the presence of a dangerous animal. Many live in isolation, but their skills are sought by scouts, merchants, explorers, and all who must cross the most hostile regions.

The most experienced develop a special bond with nature and the creatures that inhabit it. Some raise animal companions, others become true guardians of the forests they have roamed all their lives. These Masters of the Woods know every trail, every river, and every hunting ground in their domain. Where a traveler sees only a forest, they read a story written in footprints, broken branches, and the songs of animals.
SDP.Journal.Career.herbalist.Title: Herbalists
SDP.Journal.Career.herbalist.Epigraph1:
"My first master said you should always taste a plant before using it. I had to find another master after he tasted the wrong one."
— Sophianos, human collector
SDP.Journal.Career.herbalist.Intro:
Herbalists devote their lives to the study, gathering, and preservation of plants. Some roam forests, marshes, and mountains in search of rare species, while others practice their trade close to home, knowing every trail, every clearing, and every plant in their region better than anyone else. All share the same passion: understanding the countless properties of the plant world.

Their knowledge allows them to identify remedies, poisons, stimulants, and precious ingredients where most people see only simple wild herbs. Over time, they learn to recognize the changing seasons, nature's whims, and the conditions needed for the most sought-after species to grow. Their expertise makes them valuable allies for travelers, doctors, apothecaries, and isolated communities.

The most experienced botanists go beyond simple gathering to study interactions between plants, catalog unknown species, and develop their own preparations. The greatest among them become true scholars, guardians of knowledge accumulated over generations. Their gardens and collections sometimes hold specimens found nowhere else in the world.
SDP.Journal.Career.artisan.Title: Artisans
SDP.Journal.Career.artisan.Epigraph1:
"If it breaks, someone used it wrong. If it explodes, it's probably an engineer's work."
— Bromi, dwarf artisan
SDP.Journal.Career.artisan.Intro:
Artisans devote their lives to transforming raw materials into useful, durable, or admirable objects. Whether they work metal, wood, leather, fabric, or any other material, they share the same quest: to master their craft and produce quality creations.

Their trade demands patience, precision, and perseverance. Every tool, every gesture, and every technique is the fruit of years of experience accumulated in workshops, guilds, or under recognized masters. Artisans spend much of their lives perfecting their methods, learning new techniques, and solving the countless problems their trade presents.

In every society, artisans hold an essential place. Peasants need their tools, soldiers their weapons and armor, merchants their goods, and nobles their luxuries. Their work shapes the daily lives of thousands, though few realize the breadth of knowledge required to accomplish it.

The finest artisans do not merely manufacture objects. They create works capable of enduring for generations. A perfectly balanced blade, exceptional armor, or ingenious mechanism can make their creator's reputation long after death. For many artisans, true success is measured not by wealth accumulated, but by the quality of the works they leave behind.
SDP.Journal.Career.performer.Title: Entertainers
SDP.Journal.Career.performer.Epigraph1:
"If the crowd applauds, I earn my living. If it laughs, I earn my dinner. If it throws vegetables, I at least earn something to cook."
— Philétas, human bard
SDP.Journal.Career.performer.Epigraph2:
"One evening, I sang before three farmers, a dog, and a goat. The next day, the whole town knew my song. Since then, I never underestimate my audience again."
— Demetrios, human minstrel
SDP.Journal.Career.performer.Intro:
Entertainers live by their talents and their ability to captivate an audience. Musicians, storytellers, dancers, acrobats, jugglers, or actors, they travel roads and cities in search of a new stage, an attentive crowd, or a well-filled purse. Where others see a village square or a noisy tavern, they see an opportunity to perform and earn their living.

Accustomed to travel, entertainers discover the world from a particular angle. They cross paths with merchants, nobles, brigands, soldiers, and peasants, gathering stories, rumors, and anecdotes along their journeys. This wandering life teaches them to adapt quickly to their environment, understand their audience, and make the most of every situation.

While many earn an honest living from their performances, few ignore the small schemes that help make ends meet. A good entertainer knows how to amuse a crowd, but also how to spot opportunities, negotiate a favorable contract, or quietly leave a town when trouble becomes too great.

The most talented eventually acquire a reputation that precedes them. Their songs cross borders, their stories are retold in taverns, and their shows draw ever larger crowds. Some become true celebrities whose names are known far beyond the roads they travel.
SDP.Journal.Career.gladiator.Title: Gladiators
SDP.Journal.Career.gladiator.Epigraph1:
"The greater the legend, the more memorable the fall."
— Léontios, Champion Breaker
SDP.Journal.Career.gladiator.Intro:
Gladiators live by combat and spectacle. Some face their opponents in great arenas before hundreds of spectators, but most perform in improvised pits, village squares, or local festivals. Wherever a crowd is willing to pay to see blood spilled or admire a martial feat, there is often a gladiator ready to take the stage.

The rules vary enormously from one fight to the next. Some bouts require specific weapons or armor, others pit several fighters against one another in a chaotic melee. It is not uncommon to face wild animals, exotic creatures, or condemned prisoners. In the most brutal arenas, death may even be demanded to satisfy the crowd.

With each victory, gladiators gain renown, wealth, and admirers. The most famous become true living legends, acclaimed wherever they go. But in the arena, glory is fleeting: a single ill-fated bout is enough for yesterday's hero to become tomorrow's corpse.
SDP.Journal.Career.ruralworker.Title: Rural Workers
SDP.Journal.Career.ruralworker.Epigraph1:
"A good landowner knows the names of his lands. A great landowner also knows the names of the men who work them."
— Leôn, Landowner
SDP.Journal.Career.ruralworker.Intro:
The rural worker lives by the rhythm of the seasons. They cultivate the land, raise livestock, maintain roads, sometimes fell timber, and watch over the resources that allow their community to survive. Where merchants see goods and nobles see estates, they see harvests to save, animals to feed, and land to preserve.

Most rural workers begin their lives as day laborers, hiring out their strength for a few coins or a hot meal. Over the years, they learn to know the land, the beasts, and the whims of the weather. Some eventually come to own their own farm, while the most prosperous become owners of vast estates and employ in turn those who were once their peers.

Few truly understand the importance of their trade. Armies cannot march without food. Cities cannot prosper without harvests. Even the mightiest lords depend on the work accomplished every day in the fields, pastures, and farms.

Rural workers possess knowledge forged by experience rather than study. They know the seasons, animals, lands, and the countless tasks required to keep a holding running. This knowledge is rarely written in books; it is passed down through generations, over a meal, at the edge of a field, or during a long day's work. Though often underestimated by city dwellers and scholars, rural workers know that a prosperous community rests above all on those who produce what it consumes.
SDP.Journal.Career.prospector.Title: Prospectors
SDP.Journal.Career.prospector.Epigraph1:
"Every map is a confession. It reveals as much about what its maker knows as about everything they still do not know."
— Lorien, Cartographer
SDP.Journal.Career.prospector.Intro:
Few people are willing to abandon the comfort of a home to venture into regions whose dangers no one truly knows. Yet prospectors make that choice every day. Where others see impassable mountains, hostile forests, or desolate lands, they see opportunities. A forgotten vein of ore, a rare plant, a water source, a new trade route, or even a region still absent from the maps may be enough to make their fortune.

A prospector's work is above all about discovery. Some roam wild country in search of precious metals, rare stones, or resources capable of enriching an entire city. Others specialize in studying unexplored territories, drawing ever more accurate maps of known lands. Often they combine both, for a discovery is only valuable if someone can find its location again.

Despite the progress of kingdoms and cities, much of the world remains unknown. Isolated valleys, forgotten forests, unexplored mountain ranges, and lost ancient paths still await discovery. Prospectors are often the first to set foot in these regions. Some find wealth there. Others find death.

The profession attracts individuals with varied motivations. Some dream of glory and recognition. Others simply seek to sell their discoveries to the highest bidder. A few, rarer still, are driven by insatiable curiosity and pursue every horizon with the certainty that the world still hides countless secrets.

To many, prospectors are merely well-equipped wanderers. Yet every mine exploited, every road opened, and every map completed bears witness to their importance. Kingdoms grow thanks to the soldiers who defend them, but they expand thanks to the prospectors who show where to go.
SDP.Journal.Career.traveler.Title: Traveler
SDP.Journal.Career.traveler.Epigraph1:
"You see that old stone milestone? Humans think it points the right way. I know it mainly points to where bandits like to wait."
— Naeris, Elven Guide
SDP.Journal.Career.traveler.Intro:
Travelers spend their lives on the roads. Whether they drive a stagecoach, escort merchants, guide pilgrims, or carry messages from one city to another, they cover distances that few would dare attempt. By crossing plains, forests, mountains, and borders again and again, they eventually come to know the world better than most scholars.

The roads are rarely safe. Bandits, wild beasts, bad weather, and simple accidents are part of daily life. Travelers learn to anticipate danger, read the traces left along the paths, find shelter before a storm, and keep their composure when all seems lost. They also know how to care for their mounts—true partners without whom no journey would be possible.

Accustomed to meeting all kinds of people, they know the relay stations, inns, local customs, and rumors circulating from one region to the next. Many serve as guides or messengers; others prefer to live by escort work or transporting travelers. Whatever their trade, all share the same certainty: the roads reward the cautious... but never forgive the reckless.
SDP.Journal.Career.alchemist.Title: Alchemists
SDP.Journal.Career.alchemist.Epigraph1:
"The difference between a poison and a remedy often lies in the quantity... or in the intention."
— Lorien, Alchemist
SDP.Journal.Career.alchemist.Epigraph2:
"If your laboratory has never caught fire, you probably lack ambition."
— Eldrin, Master of Essences
SDP.Journal.Career.alchemist.Intro:
Alchemy is the art of transforming the world's resources into substances with new properties. Remedies, poisons, explosives, oils, perfumes, dyes, or elixirs—the creations of alchemists are as varied as the ingredients they handle. Where an herbalist often content themselves with what nature provides, the alchemist seeks to understand, alter, and improve the properties of the matter they study.

Most begin as preparators, learning to follow proven recipes and to handle sometimes unstable ingredients safely. With experience, they develop their own methods, discover new combinations, and refine their creations. The most talented become renowned distillers, able to extract rare essences or reproduce preparations that others consider impossible.

However, the profession suffers from a sometimes unsettling reputation. Alchemical research rewards experimentation, and many alchemists regard failure as a necessary step toward discovery. Some content themselves with studying plants, minerals, or animals. Others push their research much further. Experiments on living creatures are common in certain circles, and rumors sometimes speak of researchers willing to test their creations on intelligent beings to obtain more precise results. While some of these practices are condemned, others remain perfectly legal so long as they serve research or the community's interest.

This blurred line between genius and madness fuels many tales. Alchemists are admired for their discoveries, but also feared for their insatiable curiosity. For in their quest for knowledge, few things truly seem forbidden to them.

Despite this, kingdoms, armies, physicians, and merchants depend heavily on their work. Every effective remedy, every new product, and every technical advance reminds us that progress is often born from those who dare to experiment where others prefer not to look.
SDP.Journal.Career.weaver.Title: Weaver
SDP.Journal.Career.weaver.Epigraph1:
"Many see a stone capable of producing cold. I already see a cellar that will no longer spoil an entire village's harvest."
— Lethael, elf weaver
SDP.Journal.Career.weaver.Intro:
Weavers see the world differently from other mages. Where most wonder which spell to cast, they ask what an object could accomplish if endowed with the right property. A door that opens only to its owner, a lantern that shines without fuel, or a chest capable of keeping food cold are, for them, merely problems awaiting a solution.

Their work consists of understanding the properties of magic stones, then associating them ingeniously with the most suitable materials. Sometimes a simple energetic bond suffices to transmit a stone's natural qualities to an object. The most ambitious creations, however, demand far more: they require conceiving how magic must act, react, and interact with the world around it.

The most talented spend their lives imagining new uses for magic stones. Some seek to make daily life more comfortable, others pursue military or industrial applications, while a few bold minds devote their entire lives to achieving what everyone still considers impossible. After all, every invention was once merely an idea deemed unachievable.
SDP.Journal.Career.provost.Title: Provosts
SDP.Journal.Career.provost.Epigraph1:
"I have often seen the scales of justice tip. Strangely, they always fall toward the side where the gold bars are piled."
— Aelarion, Warden
SDP.Journal.Career.provost.Intro:
Lawmen are tasked with enforcing the laws of the realms they serve. From arresting criminals to reading out a sentence, they embody judicial authority and ensure order is maintained. Their training teaches them both to know the texts and to interpret them, because the same law can sometimes lead to very different decisions depending on the circumstances... or on the interests at stake.

Recognizable by their Insignia of Justice and their signet ring, they possess the authority needed to issue an official judgment wherever the laws of the realm they represent are recognized. Even abroad, their power remains valid, provided they respect the customs and procedures in force in the lands where they operate.

If justice claims to be blind, those who deliver it rarely are. Political pressure, rivalries, debts, or a simple bribe can sometimes tip the balance. There are judges of irreproachable integrity, just as there are others whose verdict can be bought as easily as a shipment of wheat. In the end, the law is never fairer than the person who enforces it.
SDP.Journal.Career.beater.Title: Beaters
SDP.Journal.Career.beater.Epigraph1:
"The best trap is not the one that holds a creature. It is the one it never feels the need to escape."
— Naeris, Beast Master
SDP.Journal.Career.beater.Intro:
Beast Masters devote their lives to understanding the creatures that populate the world. Where most see a threat or a simple mount, they discern instincts, habits, and an intelligence that can be understood—and even tamed. Their knowledge allows them to approach wild animals, capture dangerous creatures, and turn them into companions, mounts, or working auxiliaries.

Their trade leads them into deep forests as well as mountains, marshes, or arenas. Some supply war beasts to armies, others train the animals of nobles, stock menageries, or capture rare creatures for scholars and collectors. Their success relies less on strength than on patience, observation, and the ability to understand what drives each species.

Whether it is a simple sheepdog, a spirited horse, or a creature no one had yet managed to domesticate, they know that no beast is entirely unpredictable. Sometimes it is enough to learn to look at it with the right eyes.
SDP.Journal.Career.henchman.Title: Henchmen
SDP.Journal.Career.henchman.Epigraph1:
"People often think our trade is about killing. It isn't. Our trade is about making sure no one ever wants to fight us."
— Brom, Henchman
SDP.Journal.Career.henchman.Intro:
Whether protecting a rough establishment, collecting a debt, serving as an executioner, eliminating a target, or putting down a beast gone out of control, henchmen always answer with the same solution: force.

Their reputation rests as much on their power as on their ability to inspire fear. Many would rather yield at their mere presence than risk a confrontation. They seek neither glory nor honors; only the contract and the certainty that the job will be done matter.

Most live in the underworld, in the service of guilds, unscrupulous merchants, nobles, or anyone willing to pay the price asked. Some become respected executioners, others sink into organized crime, but all share the same reputation: when a Reaper is sent, negotiations are over.
SDP.Journal.Career.cavalier.Title: Cavaliers
SDP.Journal.Career.cavalier.Epigraph1:
"I have seen warriors lose their horse and keep fighting. I have never seen a true Cavalier lose their mount without losing a part of themselves."
— Lethariel, Nalorean Cavalier
SDP.Journal.Career.cavalier.Intro:
For a Cavalier, a mount is not merely a means of transport, but a battle partner. Every movement is planned for two, every maneuver rests on trust forged through years of training. Where other fighters see only a beast, they recognize an ally capable of turning the tide of a fight.

Their discipline demands as much mastery of arms as understanding of animals. They learn to guide their mount through the turmoil of battle, to exploit its speed in a charge, and to fight without ever breaking the balance that binds them. The most gifted no longer limit themselves to horses and manage to ride creatures many would deem impossible to mount.

Whether escorting convoys, leading reconnaissance, or charging at the front line, Cavaliers know that a warrior and their mount form a single weapon. As long as that trust endures, no ground lies beyond their reach.
SDP.Journal.Career.adept.Title: Cultists
SDP.Journal.Career.adept.Epigraph1:
"The oldest truths are not written in the kingdoms' books, but whispered during ceremonies that History never recorded."
— Ithilion, Hierophant
SDP.Journal.Career.adept.Intro:
Not all beliefs become religions. Some remain in the hands of a few faithful who refuse to see their traditions sink into oblivion. These men and women are the Cultists.

Keepers of a faith often little known, they perpetuate the rites, ceremonies, and teachings passed down by their cult. Their devotion may be directed toward a deity, a spirit, a sacred creature, or any other entity their faithful deem worthy of veneration. They protect its symbols, transmit its precepts, and seek to preserve its legacy, whatever trials they may face.

For a Cultist, the value of a belief depends neither on the number of its faithful nor on the recognition of the realms. It rests solely on the fervor of those who continue to keep it alive.
SDP.Journal.Career.herald.Title: Heralds
SDP.Journal.Career.herald.Epigraph1:
"The people do not always follow the one who speaks the truth. They follow the one who expresses himself best."
— Elarion, Herald
SDP.Journal.Career.herald.Intro:
Heralds make their profession of speech. Their voice carries the ideas, decisions, and ambitions of those who employ them. They announce new laws, report momentous events, defend a patron's interests, or seek to rally the population to a cause. Some travel the roads to inform the most remote villages, while others prefer the crowded squares of great cities where a few well-chosen words can be enough to shift opinion.

A good Herald does not merely speak. They observe their audience, adapt their discourse, and instinctively know which emotions to awaken in order to persuade. Depending on the circumstances, they will calm an angry crowd, inflame spirits before a battle, or deflect the suspicions of a powerful man. Their talent is so sought after that they are regularly hired by authorities, guilds, merchants, or cults—as well as by individuals with far less honorable intentions.

Many willingly change their appearance, name, or even accent in order to blend in among those they wish to convince. After all, an unknown face sometimes inspires more trust than a man already associated with another cause. For them, ideas are neither good nor bad; they simply need to be heard. And as long as there is an ear ready to listen, there will always be a Herald to give it a reason to believe.
SDP.Journal.Career.pirate.Title: Pirates
SDP.Journal.Career.pirate.Epigraph1:
"There is an old saying among elven sailors: 'When the gulls leave a merchant ship, watch the horizon... they may have spotted the black flag before you.'"
— Aelar, Elven Merchant
SDP.Journal.Career.pirate.Intro:
Pirates have renounced the laws of the realms to recognize only those of the sea. Living at the mercy of winds and currents, they attack merchant ships, plunder cargoes, and often vanish before authorities have time to organize a response. Some seek only gold, others freedom, while a few pursue a vengeance or glory that only the sea seems able to offer.

A pirate's life is harsh. Storms, disease, lack of provisions, and combat are as much a danger as warships. Every member of a crew must know how to climb the rigging, handle a vessel, fight during a boarding action, and survive long voyages. This existence forges men and women capable of adapting to any situation, but rarely leaves room for weakness.

While the realms consider them mere criminals, some ports willingly turn a blind eye to their activities as long as the holds stay full and purses keep filling. Pirates themselves often follow their own code, where loyalty to the crew matters more than written laws. For at sea, when no judge is there to deliver a verdict, only strength, courage, and trust between companions decide who will see the next sunrise.
SDP.Journal.Career.arcanist.Title: Arcanists
SDP.Journal.Career.arcanist.Epigraph1:
"Apprentices seek answers. Archmages seek better questions."
— Sylwen, Archmage
SDP.Journal.Career.arcanist.Intro:
Arcanists devote their lives to the study of all forms of magic. Where most mages choose to perfect a single discipline, they prefer to constantly broaden their knowledge in order to master as many spells as possible. In their eyes, each school has its strengths, and none deserves to be ignored.

This versatility makes them particularly sought-after practitioners. An Arcanist may be hired to heal the wounded, protect a caravan, reinforce a city's defenses, fertilize fields, entertain an assembly, accompany an expedition, or teach the foundations of magic. They adapt their talents to their employers' needs, convinced that a true mage must be capable of providing a solution to every situation.

Their thirst for knowledge constantly drives them to seek new grimoires, experiment with forgotten spells, and exchange with other practitioners, sometimes from very different traditions. Many travel the world for years to enrich their knowledge, persuaded that magic is never limited to what a single master can teach.

For an Arcanist, power is not measured by the strength of a single spell, but by the ability to understand, adapt, and master every facet of the arcane art.
SDP.Journal.Career.channeler.Title: Channelers
SDP.Journal.Career.channeler.Epigraph1:
"An Avatar crossed a battlefield without uttering a single incantation. Yet the survivors swore they had seen the arcane dance around each of his blows."
— Demetrios
SDP.Journal.Career.channeler.Intro:
Unlike most mages, who project the arcane through incantations or rituals, Channelers have chosen an entirely different path. Through meditation, discipline, and relentless training, they learn to circulate magical flows within their own bodies until every movement is imbued with them.

For them, magic is not a weapon to be wielded, but a natural extension of themselves. It strengthens their muscles, guides their reflexes, and accompanies every gesture. A parry becomes sturdier, a leap more precise, a blow more powerful. With sufficient mastery, they no longer need to distinguish the moment they fight from the moment they channel the arcane: the two become one.

This discipline was born among humans, who developed many methods of breathing, concentration, and training to master the flows coursing through their bodies. Their ideal is to achieve perfect harmony between body, mind, and magic.

The most accomplished become true Avatars. Their mastery is such that the arcane seems to respond instinctively to their movements. Their foes often believe they cast no spells at all... until they realize that every one of their blows is one.
SDP.Journal.Career.spy.Title: Spies
SDP.Journal.Career.spy.Epigraph1:
"The best disguise is not another face. It is a life so ordinary that no one thinks to mistrust it."
— Naeris, Informant
SDP.Journal.Career.spy.Intro:
Spies live in the shadow of the events they nevertheless help shape. Their trade is not to fight, but to observe, listen, and report information that others would prefer to keep secret. A merchant wishing to learn a rival's intentions, a realm watching its neighbors, or a guild seeking to protect its interests may all turn to their services.

A good spy knows how to blend into their surroundings without ever drawing attention. They adopt new identities, learn local customs, master several languages, and adapt to the people they meet until they become almost invisible. Where others would see a simple traveler, craftsman, or servant, they see the perfect cover to approach their target without arousing the slightest suspicion.

Not all intelligence is gathered through observation, however. Some secrets are won through trust, others through lies, corruption, or patience. The best spies know that truth often hides in the most ordinary conversations and that a simple rumor can sometimes be worth more than a chest full of gold.

When a mission ends, they often have only one thing left to do: disappear. For a true spy must never leave behind anything but questions.
SDP.Journal.Career.smuggler.Title: Smugglers
SDP.Journal.Career.smuggler.Epigraph1:
"A young dwarf asked me how to recognize a smuggler. I told him: 'Look for the one who knows every guard by their first name, without wearing any uniform.'"
— Thorgar
SDP.Journal.Career.smuggler.Intro:
Smugglers make their living from goods that laws forbid, tax, or reserve for a privileged few. Where guards see a border, they see only one more obstacle to circumvent. They take forgotten trails, cross marshes, navigate isolated rivers, or bribe the right people to deliver their cargo without drawing attention.

Their clientele is as varied as the goods they transport. Some deliver spices or spirits to evade taxes; others move weapons, relics, rare creatures, artifacts, or even fugitives. Many claim to be mere carriers, leaving their clients responsible for what they ship. In truth, few smugglers truly ignore the contents of their cargoes; they simply choose not to ask questions.

Their greatest wealth lies neither in their carts nor their vessels, but in the secret routes and contacts they maintain. An experienced smuggler knows which patrols to avoid, which reliable passers to trust, which inns to exchange a shipment at, and which officers will look the other way for a few coins. When a route becomes too dangerous, they find another.

The best eventually build a true network linking cities, borders, and clandestine ports. They can obtain almost any merchandise, provided one has the means. In taverns, it is often said that there are two ways to acquire a rare object: wait until it goes on sale... or know a Purveyor.
SDP.Journal.Career.leafwalker.Title: Leaf Walkers
SDP.Journal.Career.leafwalker.Epigraph1:
"Academies teach how to wield magic. The paths teach why to use it."
— Sylara Nythwen, Sage of the Seasons
SDP.Journal.Career.leafwalker.Intro:
Leaf Walkers are itinerant mages who roam the roads, forests, and forgotten trails of the world. Unlike arcanists shut away in their towers or scholars busy debating in academies, they learn their art through contact with the wind, the seasons, and the lands they cross. Their magic is intimately tied to nature and the cycles of the living world, which they regard as the greatest teachers of all.

From village to village, they offer their services in exchange for a meal, a roof, or a few coins. They heal wounded animals, soothe troubled spirits, advise farmers on coming harvests, and put their magical knowledge at the service of the communities they meet. This closeness to common folk often wins them a warm welcome where other mages inspire mistrust or fear.

Leaf Walkers spend much of their lives on the road. They learn to read the signs left by animals, recognize useful plants, and perceive the subtle changes that affect the world's magic. Many maintain a special bond with wildlife and develop an instinctive understanding of their environment that few others can match.

Over time, some become Root Weavers, able to perceive the invisible bonds that unite magic, the earth, and living beings. The wisest eventually become known as Sages of the Seasons. These rare individuals are respected in many regions, and their mere visit is sometimes considered an omen of prosperity. Over decades, they accumulate considerable knowledge of the natural world, the creatures that inhabit it, and the mysteries that still slumber in wild places.
